resources.string: Connect this phone/tablet as a USB host (OTG) to the target device’s supported device/OTG port using a data cable. Enable USB debugging on the target. A host-only TV USB port cannot be used for this connection.
Allow USB access on this device, then unlock the target and confirm its RSA debugging prompt. Authorization may take up to a minute.
This device does not support USB host mode. Use a compatible phone/tablet with OTG or a desktop computer.
USB access was denied, cancelled or timed out. Press Connect and allow access in the system dialog.
The USB device was disconnected. Reconnect the cable, refresh the list and select the device again.
Cannot open the ADB USB interface. Close other USB/ADB applications and reconnect the cable.
USB ADB communication failed. Check the data cable, USB debugging and authorization on the target, then reconnect.
Running on a TV: it will connect to this device itself.
Running on a phone: connect to a TV over the network or USB.
Cannot reach the device. Check that it is on the same network and that debugging is enabled.
The device needs pairing with a code. Open Wireless debugging on it and use pairing below.
Confirm the debugging prompt on the device screen, then try again.
The device rejected the pairing code. Codes expire quickly — open a fresh one.
Pairing timed out. Check the network and request a fresh pairing code.
Pairing could not finish. Check the pairing port and request a fresh code on the TV.
The secure connection could not be established. Check the debugging port and try again.
Pairing requires Android 10 or later on the device running this app. Classic network debugging is still available.
Connection failed for an unexpected reason.
On the TV open Developer options → Wireless debugging → Pair device with pairing code.
The pairing port and the connection port are different. Both are shown on the TV.
Devices found automatically on the network
No devices found. Make sure wireless debugging is on and its screen is open.
Network discovery is unavailable on this device. Enter the address manually.
Network discovery is unavailable. Enter an address manually; error details are available in Diagnostics.
Allow local network access to discover TVs and connect to their addresses.
Search by country code, country name or address — for example ru, by, kz. Case does not matter. Tapping a result puts the address into the field below.
A domain name (time.google.com) or an IP address (216.239.35.0) — both work.
IP: %1$s — tap to use the address instead of the name
That is not a valid server address.
The device still reports %1$s. The connection may not have permission to change secure settings.
Could not change the time server: %1$s
When connecting for the first time, the TV asks to allow debugging from this device and shows a key fingerprint. Confirm it on the TV screen — ticking “Always allow” saves you from repeating it.
Answers as a time server: %1$d ms, %2$d%% of replies, clock offset %3$s s.
Does not answer as a time server: %1$s
It answers, but reports a time that is far off. Applying it would break the clock rather than fix it.
No server answered. The network may be blocking NTP.
Up to 200 events from the last 7 days, stored only on this device.
Delete saved events and the last crash details?
History cannot be saved. Connection and time settings remain available.
Events skipped because the queue was full: %1$d
This event has expired or the journal was cleared.
The app closed unexpectedly last time. Details are available in diagnostics.
USB detected, ADB interface not found
USB host mode is not supported
ADB device found; connection has not been checked
The operation did not complete. See diagnostics for details.
The Android USB service returned an empty device list. The cause has not been determined; ADB access cannot be requested yet. Open USB connection help or Diagnostics for system details.
The system reports USB host mode. An empty device list means enumeration has not completed or the USB service is not exposing the device.
The system reports a connection in USB device mode, with host mode inactive. To control the TV, this phone/tablet needs to act as the USB host.
The system reports no USB connection in host or device mode. This status alone does not establish the cause.
The firmware did not provide enough USB role information. The role cannot be determined from an empty device list.

Refresh the list, then open the latest USB search in Diagnostics → Details. It includes device counts and system USB flags without device identifiers. System flags may be unavailable or delayed on some firmware.
Android sees a USB device but no ADB interface. Enable USB debugging on the target and reconnect the cable. If using a hub, the detected device may be only the hub.
Could not read the USB device list. Refresh it; error details are available in Diagnostics.
Devices with ADB found: %1$d. Select a device below to request access.

SHIELD without micro-USB: use port 1, furthest from HDMI. The phone must be the USB host; a regular USB-A to USB-C cable may select the opposite role. Enabling OTG alone does not guarantee a suitable connection.
The time server did not respond to the check.
The device did not confirm the time server setting.
